title: cs-field-vox-annotated-requests-digest-2029-04-10
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a rough, annotated digest of customer feedback collected from field calls, support threads, and quick surveys during March–early April 2029. The goal is to capture: 1) raw asks and representative quotes, 2) short vignettes that show why the ask matters operationally, 3) a lightweight triage (P0/P1/P2 + risk flags), and 4) suggested low-effort experiments or clarifying questions for product/eng to decide next steps.

Notes on provenance:
- Sources: 12 field calls (AM/SE-led), 28 support tickets triaged by CS ops, 4 enterprise onboarding interviews.
- Topline themes below are ordered by frequency weighted by customer ARR and mission impact (i.e., a high-touch enterprise ask > many small self-serve asks).
- These are not final product requirements — treat them as inputs for discovery.

1) "Per-route cost breakdown at token granularity" (P0)
Representative quote: "We need to see per-route token cost in the console down to the model and route level so we can make a real cost allocation for our microservices. For a few routes we're seeing wild variance and can't explain it." — Infrastructure lead, AcmeRetail
Vignette: Medium-sized e-comm client running 20 routes; CFO expects route-level unit economics for Q3 capacity planning. They currently export billing CSVs and stitch with internal logs; it’s error-prone.
Why it matters: Finance + platform teams cannot adopt Dedicated or predictable budgets without this visibility.
Suggested experiments/asks:
- Quick spike: add a per-route token breakdown CSV export (30–60m of work if existing token counters are per-request) and share with 2 pilot customers for feedback.
- UX: add a route-picker and 7-day/30-day aggregation row in Console (design suggestion attached in linked confluence).
Open questions:
- Do we have consistent token attribution when requests are proxied through function calls and reranking?
Risk flags: billing/accuracy mismatch could create charge disputes (legal involvement).

2) "Predictable fallback routing with SLAs" (P0)
Representative quote: "When our primary model saturates, we want traffic to fall back to a cheaper compatible variant without an unknown perf hit or silent quality regression." — Platform engineer, FinClear
Vignette: Financial analytics platform uses a custom embedding + reranker flow. During spikes, primary dedicated nodes hit capacity and fallback to hosted results — but semantic differences caused a production outage for a loan-assessment feature.
Why it matters: Reliability and principled fallback can prevent revenue-impacting regressions and is a top requirement for Dedicated customers.
Suggested experiments/asks:
- Define a compatibility matrix (model equivalence classes) and a simple policy: fallback_by_cost, fallback_by_latency, fallback_by-quality (quality requires eval harness).
- Build a canary test: simulate capacity drop and validate fallback route under synthetic traffic for two pilots.
Open questions:
- What telemetry thresholds should trigger fallback? (queue depth? p95 latency?).
Risk flags: silent model behavior changes if fallback isn't quality-checked.

3) "Per-customer KV/prefix caching controls" (P1)
Representative quote: "We have long-running chat sessions for a subset of enterprise customers and need to pin cache behavior per-customer to reduce tokens and latency. Global caching settings are too blunt." — Solutions engineer, MedScribe
Vignette: Healthcare SaaS uses long-context summaries; per-tenant cache eviction/TTL would drop token costs by ~25% and reduce latency for heavy accounts.
Why it matters: Cost and latency optimization for a few high-use tenants.
Suggested experiments/asks:
- Product: expose per-customer cache profile toggles in Dedicated and Private (TTL, max-prefix-length, eviction strategy).
- Short-term: allow per-api-key cache override via header for testing.
Open questions: cross-tenant cache contamination risks for Shared hosting.

4) "Eval-first rollout policy + prompt-set monitoring" (P1)
Representative quote: "When a new model or quantization is rolled, we want automated checks against our prompt sets and a regression signal that maps to business metrics." — ML ops lead, Surveyly
Vignette: Surveyly rolled q8 quantized variant and saw subtle tone shifts causing drop in survey completion. They had no automated regression alert tied to their calibration prompts.
Why it matters: Quality regressions are expensive; builds trust for automated rollouts.
Suggested experiments/asks:
- Integrate a simple hook: for any rollout, run 100 customer-specified prompts and compute a similarity/utility score; fail-fast if below threshold.
- Console: show a quick-change graph for pre/post rollout on selected prompts.
Open questions: standardizing prompt sets across customers (privacy).

5) "Private onboarding checklist gaps (network & KMS)" (P1)
Representative quote: "Last private install stalled for 3 weeks over KMS IAM roles and a weird MTU issue. We need a pre-checklist to avoid this." — Infra lead, GovHealth
Vignette: Large regulated customer delayed go-live due to network config assumptions. They asked for a pre-install checklist and a test harness.
Why it matters: Deployment friction slows sales and increases SE time.
Suggested experiments/asks:
- Create a one-page pre-install diagnostic script + checklist (KMS endpoints, firewall rules, MTU, DNS, Egress IPs).
- Offer a 1-hour pre-install session as a paid add-on or success play.
Open questions: which checks are automatable vs manual?

Low-frequency but high-severity asks (P2/P1)
- Granular embedding vector sizing options (customers want 384 vs 1k vectors configurable per-route).
- SLO-aware SDK client that hints routing preference (latency-first vs cost-first).
- Exportable, annotated error traces (per-request) for compliance audits.

Raw quote appendix (unfiltered)
- "If we can tag routes to teams and get daily cost emails for each, we can finally stop exporting CSVs." — Eng manager, PixelCart
- "We would pay for a preflight test that validates on-prem hardware compatibility." — CTO, SecureBank
- "Latency spikes at p95 only during mid-month billing runs, we suspect background jobs are saturating GPU pools." — Platform ops, AdOptimize

Immediate recommended next steps (for PM + Eng sync)
- PM: choose 2 P0 asks (Per-route cost breakdown + Predictable fallback routing) for discovery this sprint. Owner: Maya.
- Eng: quick feasibility spike for per-route CSV export and a small proof-of-concept fallback policy (owner: Diego).
- CS: nominate 3 pilot customers for each spike, collect exact acceptance criteria (owner: Priya).
- Ops/SRE: identify billing attribution edge-cases (owner: Jordan).

Decision log / Outstanding decisions:
- Do we treat per-route cost as billing-grade (requires invoicing changes) or exploratory visibility only? (Decision due: Apr 20)
- Fallback policy: conservative default to avoid silent quality regressions. Need SRE/ML sign-off.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Attach sample CSV schema and minimal UI mockups to the Confluence page (Maya)
- Schedule 30-min discovery with FinClear and AcmeRetail next week to validate fallback acceptance tests (Priya to arrange)

End of digest.
(Informal: file is noisy — meant for internal triage. Use as input to PRD skeleton, not final spec.)
